title: ENABLE 2 Remote Care - Digital coordination and recording of patient satisfaction, quality of life (HRQoL) and patient-reported adverse events in breast cancer
summary: Treatment for primary breast cancer depends on the molecular subtype of the tumor tissue and is administered in the form of chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, anti-HER2 antibody therapy, or a combination or sequence of these therapies, either adjuvantly or neoadjuvantly. Current studies are also testing the use of immunotherapies in (neo-)adjuvant settings in high-risk populations. Furthermore, the first personalized therapy trials are being initiated, testing the use of innovative off-label therapies in the post-neoadjuvant setting in patients with a high risk of recurrence or metastasis. With the individualization of tumor therapy, side effect management is also becoming increasingly complex. Immunotherapies, in particular, require close monitoring and timely detection of initial symptoms to avoid serious long-term consequences for patients. Early detection of loss of quality of life and the occurrence of intolerable side effects to improve treatment adherence are key challenges in adjuvant breast cancer therapy. Psychological symptoms and impaired quality of life can occur even years after primary treatment and have a significant impact on the quality of life and ability to work of those affected.

interventions.name: Intervention group: Weekly EQ-VAS surveys with a subsequent intervention algorithm, in addition to the HRQoL surveys linked to the therapy.
Control group: baseline visits (PRO, questionnaires in special therapy situations) at fixed times.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
● Computer, tablet, or mobile phone with internet access.
● Invasive breast cancer or metastasis of breast cancer and neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT).
● Capacity to consent.
● Signed informed consent and agreement to the data protection regulations.
● The inclusion criteria for the accompanying feasibility and usability study are identical. However, study staff (e.g., physicians, study nurses, other relevant staff) can also be included.
Exclusion criteria:
● Patients who, according to the treating physician, cannot reasonably be expected to participate in the study due to a severely limited life expectancy or serious comorbidities.
● Patients who, according to the treating physician, are not suitable for informed consent and cooperation due to psychological or cognitive limitations.
● Patients who have not signed the consent form or do not agree to the data protection regulations.
● The exclusion criteria for the accompanying study on feasibility and usability are identical.
